utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Before we begin, the Chamber is aware that the accused has requested access to a note verbal filed in this case on the 8th of October, on a confidential basis, an ex parte basis. The Chamber sees no reasons why the accused should not receive a copy of that note verbal with the passport details of the relevant witness redacted and therefore request the Registry to make such a redacted copy available to him. Let's continue your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope I will simplify my questions today in order to receive yes or no answers as much as possible so that you can travel and leave soon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have in e-court 1D2571 so as that we finalise this portion that has to do with the streets, or rather, the names of the streets. 1D2571.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- do you agree, Mr. Sabljica, that Hamdije Kresevljacka [phoen] street, which is fourth from the bottom, was Jawaharlal Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Hamdije Kapidzica, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document tendered into evidence and finished with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Again, we received this document about 25 minutes ago. We're not entirely sure as to the integrity of this particular web site. We also note that it's not visible on the screen at the moment, but at the bottom of this document there is a -- actually, that's all right. There's a reference to a first name of a witness who is not protected, but we haven't had an opportunity to check the integrity of this web site in any way, and with that caveat, I leave it to Your Honours' discretion as to whether you wish to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will go to the weight or the probative value at the end of the day, but I don't see any problem admitting this. But let me consult with my colleagues first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D747, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you remember, Mr. Sabljica, yesterday we discussed incident number 6 from G list of the 22nd of January, 1994, Alipasino Polje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have document that we saw yesterday on our screen which is 65 ter 09609.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting, can we both agree that none of the warring parties had silencers for mortars?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I wasn't part of the crews working on mortars, but let's say that it was not possible to hear the shells falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there is no such device that can be attached to the barrel of the mortar?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far can one hear the outgoing fire for 82 and for 120 approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean how far you have to be from the firing position in order to hear the shell being fired?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you from my personal experience while I was in the army at the beginning of the war. It was very close, between 50 and 100 metres, and you can then hear the shell being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that we need a different page from this one. It's the report that you received in hard copy. I need a photograph. Just give me a moment, please. Page 2, that's what we have here -- no, that's page 1 but we need page 2. Do you still have this report with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the hard copy? No, I don't have it. I can see it on the screen only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which shells landed there in this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two 82-millimetre shells and one 120-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that established by your team or did you receive this information from someone else?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our team established the traces for the two 82s and the information concerning the 120-millimetre shell were received from the policemen and the witnesses, but the presumption was that it landed on a roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which roof?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of a building, that's the information we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it did not create a crater in the ground; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. We couldn't find its traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On what basis did they decide that it was 120-millimetres because it did not land on the ground, but I suppose that it exploded above the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It allegedly landed on the roof of a skyscraper and exploded there; that was the information that we had. I believe that another shell fell in the park on the grass, but as far as I can remember we did not carry out an on-site investigation of that particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to tell us if you saw the photographs of that site, have they ever been made, and why they are missing from the file?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see the photograph and I know that they were made by the scene of crime officer. I'm not going to tell his name because I don't know if he's a protected witness. He worked with the late Stankov and me, he fixed the traces of the shell, and he prepared the whole set of documents. I believe that in the previous case where I testified, the photographs were attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a photograph of the shell that fell between the streets at Klare Cetkin and Rade Koncar?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that the 120-millimetre shell was not photographed. It landed on grass. The only ones that were processed were the two that fell on the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As a ballistics expert, do you believe that in order to establish the direction and the angle, the one that landed in the park would have been more suitable for that purpose rather than the other two?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the opposite because the traces on a hard surface are more visible, particularly with regard to shrapnel. I explained that yesterday. Craters can look differently, but you can apply a different method if you find an unexploded tail fin or the fuse of the shell on the spot. In most cases the shell fell on hard concrete surfaces, and in that cases we applied the method of the central axis which was a more accurate one. So we didn't do this one and I don't think there were any casualties caused by the one that fell in the park.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you think that was the reasons. So I think that the furrow would be very helpful in order to determine the angle and the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree with you because this method is applied on the battleground as well because the expert there can very simply and very accurately establish the origin of fire by applying this so-called tunnel method that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this was done by your team or by some other team, but it was established that this shell that fell on Cetinjska street came from the west from Nedzarici from the institute for the blind. Does that mean that this westerly direction has the bearing of around 270?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean with regard to north, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly at this moment. The report says only that it came from the westerly direction, from Nedzarici and the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 1, paragraph 3. It says: "Upon inspection of the site on the Cetinjska Street and the surface, an existence of a central crater was established with the ellipsis axis of 15 and 20 centimetres and the crater about 6 centimetres. The central part of the crater stretches ellipse-wise into star-shaped traces, this ellipse being 110 and 180 centimetres long. The longer sides of the ellipses run east-west, the distance from the centre of the crater to the west being longer. Given that the axis of a falling shell forms an angle of less than 90 degrees ..." So we can all see this now. Says without reading the whole paragraph, the penultimate sentence reads: "This direction is where Nedzarici is located, i.e., the Institute for the Blind. One person was killed by the impact of the shell ..." And so on and so forth. So it was established that in this direction the institute was located which means that -- and let's look at the previous sentence which says: "On the basis of the traces visible on the asphalt road surface where the shell landed and the shapes of the visible traces and the traces left by blast, it is possible to conclude that the shell was an 82-millimetre mortar shell fired from a westerly direction. This direction is where Nedzarici is located, i.e., the Institute for the Blind." Isn't it true that it wasn't established from where the shell came, that only a general westerly direction was established, where the Institute for the Blind in Nedzarici is located?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I said yesterday that by applying the methods that we had at our disposal, we were not able to establish the exact place of the origin of fire. We only gave a general direction which involved Nedzarici and the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me remind you then yesterday we established and in this document it says that the westerly direction or a little bit towards north-west, that wouldn't then constitute 270, the bearing should be slightly different; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: West-north-west, let me say that that's this slight deviation and it indicates Nedzarici and that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you remember that on that map we saw yesterday we saw that Nedzarici were a little bit to the south and a little bit to the north were dormitory and the Oslobodjenje building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We marked that on that map yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on someone from that team comes to a conclusion. You mentioned that person's name. As far as the shell that fell in the park between Klare Cetkin and Rade Koncar, it can be established that it was fired to the west of Nedzarici and the Institute for the Blind. That is all contained in that report; isn't that right? I can give you the line?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it's on the next page, that is written there, it's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, actually we can skip some questions because you've already spoken about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that map again, the one that Mr. Sabljica marked yesterday. 746. P746.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D746.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, if you don't know exactly where the line was we will have to call up another document. Just tell us whether you know exactly where separation line was here, and if you don't know then we're going to call up another document.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where it was exactly, it was somewhere around the student dormitories, around the Oslobodjenje building. There were these barracks behind the Oslobodjenje building, but I think that that was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. That is already Nedzarici. As far as this theatre of war is concerned, I did not really go there very often except for occasional on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember witness answered that question and said that which building was whose control at the time. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. But it is important for me to establish where the line of separation was. So could we then have this map, section 9, please. 65 ter 09390C, section 9. It's the same section but the separation lines are marked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that area, Mr. Sabljica, over here by number 86 on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. The student dormitories like two Ys, the Oslobodjenje building, Nedzarici, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map where the Institute for the Blind is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. I think that it is the building marked number 13. See, I put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark it some way, say B.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: B, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: B for blind.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the line of separation is quite near to this and that fire could be registered by the other side -- actually, the soldiers of the other warring party, that is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the line of separation is nearby. Now, you're saying that it can be registered as having been fired from either side. The only thing I can say is that the line of separation is nearby, and I repeat that our reports never dealt with that, who fired the shell, from which positions, et cetera, because we did not have proper methods for establishing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just place the date -- actually, can you mark Oslobodjenje and the student dormitories on this map as well quite simply so that the participants can know where they are whenever they look at the map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, SD, student dormitories. And over here it's the Oslobodjenje building, O.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you sign it, can you put the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D748, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that one cannot see the Institute for the Blind from that site? There is no visibility, bearing in mind how high the buildings are, the ones that you're familiar with? Something must have been interpreted the wrong way. Let's see.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to repeat it for the transcript. Do you agree -- or rather, what can you say from the actual site, is there visual contact with the Institute for Blind Children, bearing in mind the buildings that we are both very familiar with, the buildings at Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no visual contact. It is impossible to see that particular site.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2245.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this kind of visual contact would be possible from the Oslobodjenje building, especially from the northern student dormitory?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree. It is very hard to see that as well from the student dormitory and the Oslobodjenje building as far as I am familiar with that part of town.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2245 then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this complex of buildings? Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Polje. It's not Alipasino.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is this neighbourhood in view of this line of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right by the separation line. That is to say it is very close to the institute for blind children and Nedzarici, say 200 or 300 metres away from it, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the east of this is that complex of buildings, one number 8 and then the other number 8 where the incident occurred, the so-called building of the neighbourhood of Alipasino Polje; right? Moving from the west, the Institute for Blind Children, Vojnicko Polje, the buildings that we see, that is, and then one number 8 of Alipasino Polje, and then the other number 8 of Alipasino Polje where the incident actually occurred; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This doesn't have to be marked, right? But I would like to have it admitted -- or actually, should it be marked? I would like this picture to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D749, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should Mr. Sabljica initial it or something? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2246, can we have that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this building? Is that the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the building of the Institute for Blind Children in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you need the map or can you confirm that in this direction that is shown by the arrow that Alipasino Polje is there, that is to say that neighbourhood to the east of this in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need a map. I can confirm that. I know that Alipasino Polje is in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree as regards that map you saw that practically in the very corner the Institute for Blind Children is semi-encircled, say about 300 degrees, that is to say on three out of four sides it is exposed to the line of separation? Let's not return the map if you do recall where it is in that corner?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember. You are right. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. We cannot hear the speakers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that it would be unusual to place mortars someplace like that, two at that 120 and 80, and to have them fire from the line itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could agree with that statement as well; however, I would like to note that we mentioned the Institute for Blind Children as one of the prominent features in Nedzarici. And again I'm saying that we could not say with any certainty where the shell had been fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D750.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have any of the tail fins been found? Do you remember -- did you remember hearing about that from those who had arrived before you? Were there any tail fins; and if so, from which calibre?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember that. If that's what's written up in our findings, that we had found tail fins, then we found them. That is always written if so. If it is not written there, then that was not the case. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that report it says that they were found. One stabiliser 120-millimetres in line 8 and those of 82 were not found. So now it's a bit of a problem. How can one conclude that there was 82-millimetres as well? Is there any certainty in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is written that such traces were found, then that is correct. As for mortar shells of 82 millimetres, that is stated clearly in the report that was signed by the late Stankov, that on the basis of the traces of destruction and looking at the axes of the irregular ellipse that was created when the shell fell on the asphalt surface, we could establish that that was the case, that it involved that mortar. I think that that is what is written there. You read that a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. It was established there that there's a central crater and that the length of the ellipses were 15 and 20 centimetres and that the axis was between 110 and 180 centimetres; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those are the two irregular ellipses that are formed in the centre of the crater, the thing that I drew yesterday, there's a smaller one and the bigger one, and the bigger one assists you in establishing the origin of fire; that is to say, the direction from which the shells had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a bit of patience, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can skip a certain number of questions now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D09606, page 2. The first one should be identified, so the 65 ter number is 09606.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly whether you remember how wide Cetinjska and Klare Cetkin are, those two streets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The width of the streets?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The standard width in Sarajevo, two lanes for cars, although both are one-way streets. However, there is a round-about after that -- anyway, it's safe enough for two cars to pass by and also there's a sidewalk for pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's about 6 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2 of this document. Something seems to be wrong. 1D2 -- can we have 02161. I can't see the ERN number on this photograph and that is a difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how these streets are orientated?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the next page of this document actually. Now we see the ERN number. The next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Sabljica, Cetinjska is what, west-east, what? Do you remember how they are orientated, these streets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Viewed from this vantage point, I think it is north-south. It goes along a semicircle by that 8, so it is the direction in which the vehicles are, north-south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this photograph and this actual site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this actual site. I'm looking at the photograph now and, yes, I remember the site, I remember this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the red car there on the right-hand side, the one that is next to this row of parked vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a red Golf, so you're not talking about the one next to the pedestrian on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am talking about the one that is on the street.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the other red car and you see where the sidewalk starts, so we can see now how wide the street is, and it roughly corresponds to what you had said, say 6 metres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be it, that standard width. It's not some kind of a big street. It's a standard street for normal traffic within a neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In view of what we see now in the middle of the photograph, do you think that this could be actually 7 metres wide?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since you see a parking-lot on one side of the street along the driveway, possibly. It's my rough estimate based on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you on this photograph - and that's a contemporaneous photograph from the time of the events, 22nd January; right? It's in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a photograph from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On that photograph could you mark the traces and the longer axis of the central crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't. I can't even see where the shell fell. I can't see anything on this photograph because this is a broader view of the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters. Do you see this arrow indicating the crater? It's not very clearly visible but it's there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this black arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that arrow indicates the crater. Is there any text under the photograph that would help?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we raise this sheet a bit, perhaps we could see the text under the photograph. It says the same as in the previous photograph. Can we get the previous photograph, number 45, to see the text, not the photo. It's the same photograph from a different angle. Can you see the site of explosion of the shell in Cetinjska Street near number 3?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we revert to the next page again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the snow to the right of this photograph, do you see any fragments?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the centre of the explosion here, I will mark it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could zoom-in a bit more on the crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, why don't we zoom-in first before the witness marks. Why don't we zoom-in a bit further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, may I ask you to mark the centre of the crater and the longer axis.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the centre and the longer axis is this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you to write the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not make this photograph, somebody else did and gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the scenes of crime officer made this photograph and it's part of our documentation together with our report. Photo documentation is made by scenes of crime officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is a certain perspective here in view of the distance from which the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in terms of approach to photography? Yes, there is a perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that perspective makes it more difficult to establish direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, but a direction is not established based on photographs; that's also a very important fact. We did not use photographs to determine directions, we used exact methods on the site; that is to say, firm traces on surfaces, not photographs. Working with photographs and drawing on photographs can give you completely different results.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have this photograph admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D751, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you use three or more sticks in this case as well? Can you remember which method was used?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, the same method of the central axis was used to determine alignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else investigate this incident to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we revert to the previous photograph, the same document but number 45. The ending of the ERN number is 745. Could we zoom-in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this photograph and draw the longer axis on this photograph. Do you see traces of fragmentation on the snow?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark the centre of the explosion here as indicated by the arrow, but it would be difficult with the axis because I'm telling you again it's very easy to make a mistake doing that on a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that on the snow you can see this rose shape, the traces of fragments on the snow?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see this aura against the -- on the snow, this halo shape in black.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would it have been better if the snow had been cleared before the photograph was made because the fragments would have left traces on the Tarmac?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would have been better. I believe there are photographs taken after the site was cleared and cleaned and sticks were put in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Chamber ask perhaps if photographs are available with the snow cleared? We haven't found them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has no clue. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will talk to the other side and ask for them because we really need everything available for each incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone inform you that the UNPROFOR also investigated the same incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't informed and my team wasn't informed, but I know they almost often did. It was part of their job.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be received as well although it isn't marked? Or perhaps it is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it's part of Prosecution Exhibit P1697.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now get 65 ter 10558, to see that UNPROFOR report on the same incident. 10588. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I say that you know English rather well. Could you look at this page on the right-hand side where the UNPROFOR describes the elements of the same incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this shelling report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Do you agree it says there were three shells and the other elements? Can you see they indicate that all three shells were 120 millimetres as well as the angle of fall, the angle of approach --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maximum range. I see all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this report suggests?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it suggests since this was done by someone from the expert UNPROFOR team. I can only see they suggest there were three shells, all three of 120 millimetres. They established angles of approach and angles of fall, and they indicate that the maximum range according to their estimate is between 2.000 and 3.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there any difference between your report, the report of the BH MUP and this report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously. They only mention 120-millimetre shells and not 82 millimetres. And they also express their findings in mils and they did not determine directions according to north-south or west-east, but the description of events is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the differences are in calibre and the possible direction of origin?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say anything accurate about the direction because it's not indicated, but I can see that there is a difference in calibre because they only mentioned three shells of 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about these mils, do you see a major difference there or should we go deeper into analysing this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to see the next page because they may have written something more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not measure the angle of fall. They measured it as 1100?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The angle of approach is between 4.200 mils and 4.250?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only determined it relative to the azimuth of a normal compass and 1 mil is about 17 degrees so you need to calculate this as far as I remember the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish the weather conditions? They say it was foggy and the temperature was 5 degrees centigrade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a standard form of an UNPROFOR report. We never mentioned in our reports the weather conditions, whether it was windy or foggy or snowing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that 1 degree is 17 mils?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said a moment ago. In fact, it's 16.85.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have time to go deeper into this, but I'd like to have this document received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The witness wanted to see the next page. Would you like to see it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, we won't insist on this because there's no time to go deeper into analysis. The fact is there is a difference in direction and if we had time I would go into it. But never mind. On some other occasion when we have someone from the UNPROFOR perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D752, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I just note at this stage before we go any further that the translation in English -- the word thousandths should actually read mils, m-i-l-s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get 1D02440. The Defence expert team visited this site on the 18th September 2010. It's in Klare Cetkin Street which is now called Bosanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this photograph it could be anywhere in the city of Sarajevo because I can't see the buildings around, so I couldn't even tell you in which part of town it is based on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that this crater here is right next to the pavement. One bit of the pavement even had to be replaced and repaired.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that these outer fragments reach almost to the middle of the street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Relative to the centre of the crater you can see it going halfway to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you draw the longer axis based on this photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if the witness is not able to confirm what place that this is about, there's no point going further, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We should have a total view in order to locate it, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These outer fragments are almost 3 metres away?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this photograph, what you say seems to be correct. But as the President says, I cannot even determine where this is so it means nothing if I draw a central axis and mark the traces because the impact of this shell could have been anywhere in town. Do you understand? You can't tell based on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I understand completely. We failed to provide a total picture to locate this place, but we won't have this admitted until someone comes to identify it. Correct. After the break we shall try to find a total view of this place and then we can deal with the photograph. Can I ask you now to try and recollect Alipasino Polje was in the area of responsibility of which brigade of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? That was your right-hand neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names of the brigades changed names four or five times. I really couldn't tell you which one was in Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you know that the 5th Motorised Brigade was later renamed 155th and that was the -- deployed in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that they were in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they always had minimum 3.000 and maximum 5.000 men? We can find that in the documents from the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that figure. I thought there were more of them. Since this was military information I had no access to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now deal with incident number 4 from G list involving the football-match that took place on the 1st of June, 1993. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't working in the police at that time. If you recall the first day of my examination, I know that this incident was investigated after the war along with Mr. Hecke and the late Medjedovic. We analysed the craters a couple of years after the incident because on the 1st of June I was still a member of the Army of BH. I don't remember it. I only heard stories. Based on our investigation, the only thing what we did was to demonstrate to the ICTY investigator how we determined the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's right. So that was conducted on the 21st of November, 1995. Do you remember what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dayton Accords were signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's correct, but that's also my family's patron saint's day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have document 09970. This patron saint's day is the Saint Archangel Michael who has been celebrated by all faiths.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1699.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the first page of your report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's part of the photo file compiled as you can see by Mr. Medjedovic and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In attendance were witness Refik Sokolar and representatives of the OTP Jan van Hecke; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about this Mr. Refik Sokolar.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You're asking me now but I can't remember him at all. It says here that he was a witness and I suppose that he was there when the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you think it's acceptable that he was a police officer from Dobrinja who was close to the explosion in the queue for water on Spasenija Babovic street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Really, this is the first time that I'm hearing about this from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of February, 1995, he was wounded in this incident and he also was present during this incident. Don't you find it a little bit odd for a police officer to be present during two similar incidents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not for him to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please cast a glance on what Mr. Medjedovic and you wrote here as the main authors of this document, so I hope this will refresh your memory and then I will proceed with my question. Can you say in paragraph 5 --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to the witness Refik Sokolar, two artillery shells fell on the parking-lot at 1000 hours on the 1st of June ... while a soccer game was taking place ..." Et cetera, et cetera. I see that the name of this witness is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the whole page now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask Mr. Gaynor because we are going to work with hard copies to provide those because this statement starts from 043658 and also there's our pages that belong as an integral part of this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As it happens, I do have an unmarked hard copy. I would be happy to give it over. That's not to say, I wish to set a precedent in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can work with both the screen and this other thing, but then it will be too small and we will not be able to see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the size of the football ground or football-pitch where this match was played?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that we measured it, but let's assume that this is a parking-lot. I don't know the exact size. I wouldn't like to second-guess.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have on our screens 1D2569.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any other playground designated as such close or next to the parking-lot as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a heating plant, and I don't know whether there was any other playground. I honestly cannot remember. This was taking place on this parking-lot close to the heating plant and the street - what's it called?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the location?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the contemporaneous photograph taken recently?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say. If I can see the heating plant nearby, then I can confirm because we wrote in our report that the heating plant is north-west from the playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the heating plant here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot. You can see it in the photo file that we prepared. It's a white building and it's a heating plant situated in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the previous document so that we can deal with these photographs. So that was 09970 and I think that we need pages 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement of the 20th of June, 2001, we'll see it later, Ismet Fazlic, the referee, said that the pitch was made of concrete and the size was 30 by 15 metres. Does that correspond to what you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about it and I don't know who this referee was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 10042, page 3. We'll keep the photographs and then on the right-hand side photograph -- on the right-hand side of the screen we need 10042. Page 3. That's the statement of Ismet Fazlic. Now page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says on page 1 that he was the referee during that game. Let's look at paragraph 4, line 4 from the top. It says that the pitch was made of concrete approximately 30 by 15 metres. In the half of the pitch where the shell detonated, all the players from both team were gathered except for the goal keeper from the other side. The spectators were also gathered at that end.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why you're asking me about this incident. I was with the police at the time -- I wasn't with the police at the time, so I think you should ask him to confirm and corroborate this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree. I just wanted to establish the size of this parking-lot that served as a football-pitch on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at these photographs and close-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to your recollection, is that part of the investigation material?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see this building east of the pitch and then to the west you can see the white building of the heating plant, and this is this parking-lot where we conducted our on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which of the two photographs is relevant?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're both relevant. It's a general view which indicates the location of the heating plant and these other buildings. So this is a general view of the site. And then we use the photographs in order to explain in more detail the methodology that we applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which of these two photographs can we see the impact spot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 shows the impact location much better. Now you can see this rose, the central crater, and you can see an officer or a soldier standing there in the corner. If you wish me, I can put a circle around the place of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you would be so kind. The place of impact and the longer axis.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the impact place, but based on this photograph it is difficult to indicate the axis. But I suppose that this is the longer axis. Although we again have the perspective in the photo as you said before, which makes it difficult to determine the origin of fire of shells. This is a totally unreliable method for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there any photographs in the investigation file that can show these elements?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have hard copies of the photographs that portray close-ups of the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate the orientation, or rather, indicate north, west, east, and south with respect to the heating plant?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the north would be approximately in this direction because the heating plant is north-west of the playground. So judging from north it is over 100 degrees of bearing when you determine the direction from which the shell arrived, and this is consistent with our report. Since there were no war operations at the time, it was possible to conduct an on-site investigation according to a proper police standard without fearing any incident taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that a problem that this took place two or three years later?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, three and a half years, I would agree with you, one has to take into consideration a series of circumstances that led to that decision. But don't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please initial this photograph -- but according to what you have drawn here it seems that on north-east rather than north-west is where the heating plant is located.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the north-west. Maybe I marked it wrongly, but I cannot draw any other conclusions on the basis of this photograph. But nevertheless, I will sign it and put the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the next page which will show the rose of the impact place much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so after admitting this one. This will be Exhibit D753.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation whether this match was played on the playground or on the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understood it, they played the game on the parking-lot. So you can see it in the photograph itself, and this is what this referee referred to 30 by 15 metres. This is his assessment as to the size, so that was an asphalt surface on which we worked. I can tell you only that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, these are the photographs that you found three and a half years later and you made markings with a white chalk?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, photograph 3 follows photograph number 2, where one can see more clearly the blast traces on the surface, and this measuring band shows the dimension of these regular ellipses and on the photograph beneath it we use the chalk to mark the poles and we used the sticks as I explained yesterday, and I explained to the Chamber yesterday how we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is oriented towards the north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see north and you can see this reddish stick which indicates the direction from which the shell arrived, which according to us is 110 degrees bearing. And this is what is stated in our report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we zoom out so that we can see both pictures. Mr. Sabljica, are we seeing the same crater from the same direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's the same crater from the same direction; however, the measure band has been moved and as you can see it's above the sticks and it depicts the north. It is not used as a measuring band now. It is an aid, as it were, to indicate where the north is. The view is the same, but in number 4 it's more of a close-up from a photography point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If it is convenient, we will take a break now for 20 minutes. We'll resume at 10.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In respect of the earlier photo, could we please see now 1D2567.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We owe you the -- this is not the document I meant. 1D2576, 1D2576, it should be a photo, and it is something that has to do with the earlier case, the Alipasino Polje that we owe you still.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, would you agree with me that this is the spot and that below the tree on the wall we can see that there is a plaque which is actually a memorial plaque to the victims?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that memorial plaque and that is the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put a circle around the memorial plaque.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For all of you in the courtroom, this is the incident 6 on the G list.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will put an SP, "spomen-ploce," memorial plaque, next to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please just mark -- indicate the portion of the sidewalk which has been replaced.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it. Here, I'll write a T for sidewalk, "trotoar" in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please date and put your signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, before he does so Mr. Karadzic just asked him if this was the spot. Perhaps it would be better at this stage to clarify which particular spot this refers to because there are three shells involved in this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assume that this is the place where the children who were sledding were killed in the Klare Cetkin Street, what it used to be called, and this is the only place in Alipasino Polje where there is a memorial plaque. So I believe that that is that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that this is -- can you recognise, actually, that this is a photo taken from a different angle as compared to the earlier photo that I showed you that you said you couldn't really recognise it and that it could be any place anywhere in the city?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could we please --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we don't have to look at the other photo. I can see that it's the same place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D754. And would you like to bring back the photo, 1D2440?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but before that I would like to also tender another photo. That's the photo taken from outside this building, 1D2577 that was. I would like to tender that one into evidence as well. 1D2577, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you now recognise the heating plant at Alipasino Polje and this same spot, a portion of the sidewalk that had been replaced and also the pavement that was repaired?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but now it's taken from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this photo was taken from outside the building where -- bearing the memorial plaque?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree based on the replacement of the sidewalk I could agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in relation to the major axis, or rather, the angle of approach, the heating plant is to the north-west?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I mentioned the heating plant in relation to the other case, the Dobrinja case. I did not mention the heating plant in relation to this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is -- the heating plant is there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but it wasn't relevant to this incident as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now please tell us whether this measuring band was placed in the way that you would place the band to indicate the major axis?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we did mark all the traces and based on the photograph it is my assumption that this could be indicating the direction from which the projectile had come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please put your signature and date on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not necessary. We will admit this, Exhibit D755.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness just please mark -- could he just mark the outer-most pockmarks, the fragment traces, and then we can go back to the photograph. So can he just sort of put a circle around the farthest marks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what we can see in the photo at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please sign this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for reference, could you circle the power-plant just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean this white band, the central axis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I don't know. You said power-plant is visible from this picture. I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Heating plant, the heating plant.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Here, T for "toplana," heating plant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could put the date your signature, and then we will admit it as Exhibit D755.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, no objection to the admission of this photograph or the previous photographs. I simply want to note that these were made available to the Prosecution at 10.40 a.m. today, which is about 12 minutes ago. I don't know of any reason why these could not have been notified to the Prosecution at the commencement of the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. When was the photo 2440 disclosed to you? Which the witness was not able to confirm when shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That one was on the list --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That one was on the list which was made available at the commencement of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These two pictures could have been disclosed at the same time then?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll note that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have again the photo marked as 1D25440, 1D02440 -- but for your information we did not want to offer a lot of photographs here. But as the witness could not confirm the general area because the photo was a close-up, as it were, that's the only reason that we also offered these photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can understand that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see now in the background the garbage containers and this is the general area that we could see in that wider photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear to me now based on the photo we had just seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please just make the arcs and just indicate how far the fragment traces went.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will but I have to stress again that a photo is not really the appropriate way to determine these things, but here it is. I will now mark the outer-most traces and then connect them to the centre and then the central axis would run approximately this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these fragments reach almost halfway into the street, which is 6- to 7 metres wide?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, viewed from this angle, that's what it looks like. But what we should really do is take a measuring tape and then go to the spot and actually measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now help us here with orientation. Can you tell us the sides of the cardinal points, where they would be?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes I can. The south is in the direction of this grey Mercedes. Of course north would be the opposite and then west and east each way -- well, I can actually indicate it here. I will put the compass rose mark and approximately it goes this way. North, east, west, and -- I'm sorry, it goes this way, south, north -- [In English] West, east, north, south. [Interpretation] To the south we have Mojmilo hill, and the north -- the north is the other way, this is the main axis. And then there is Nedzarici, and towards the east you would go down-town to the old part of town. Should I sign this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. Your signature and date, as usual.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this and this will -- we will close on this topic with this witness with this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D756, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to that football-match, incident number 4 on the G list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 1D2578, please. And my apologies to Mr. Gaynor for uploading this just recently, and the need arose because we wanted to help the witness to better find his bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise what is shown in this photo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where this would be. Maybe in Dobrinja somewhere or could this be Mojmilo? But I think that's not where this happened, this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please indicate Mojmilo, could you mark it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, is this Mojmilo hill? I wasn't sure whether I recognised it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will put an arrow here and put an M to indicate Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see the hoop here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, the basketball hoop. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what we see in the foreground, is that the playground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please put a PG there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Knowing all this, is it true that there was a match played on this parking-lot full of vehicles based on what you were told?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this photo I can't really confirm that because I cannot see either the heating plant or the building that should be someplace here at the bottom of the photograph. But if I were to be shown the heating plant then I could confirm and tell you whether this is in fact the playground in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is Mojmilo hill and this is a playground; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. You can see that in the photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please put your signature and date on the photo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have 2569, please, 1D2569.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a photo that we've seen before I believe. This is a photo which we used when we talked about dimensions. Now, would you agree with me that this basketball court is some 10 to 15 metres away from the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean where the white car is parked where we can see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, where the basketball match or the football-match was played?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't confirm again based on this photo, and I cannot confirm that that was the place of the incident based on these two photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I will now tell you what the referee and the person who organised this match said, Ismet Fazlic, in his report on the 20th of June, 2001. He said: "The second shot exploded some 10 to 15 metres away from the playground in the parking-lot." That's 65 ter 10042 page 3, paragraph 5 of his statement. This statement of his, would you agree with me, actually just creates more confusion as to where this match was played, whether it was on the playground or in the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on his statement, yes, it is unclear where this match was played; but based on the photos that you've shown me, I can't really tell whether it was indeed there because we placed this whole incident and we orientated ourselves in terms of the Hedo Maglajlic [phoen] street and the heating plant. So if you could show me one of those two landmarks that would help me because you said yourself that this on-site investigation was conducted three years later, and when we arrived with the investigators we were told that the football-match had been played there and that we should conduct a ballistics expertise based on the traces that were left by a mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My apologies. Just a moment. Can we look at this paragraph number 5 on this page, page 3, where he says: "The second shell," that's line 3, paragraph 5. Let's just look if we can find that place. It says "the second shell." I can see it in B/C/S. "The second shell exploded about 10 or 15 metres away off the playing surface, on the parking-lot." Do you agree with me that the organiser of this match and the referee actually mentioned two different areas, the playing surface and the parking-lot as two different areas?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you because that's what it says there in the statement, so I can't really contest that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they tell you how the teams had been made up, how many members on each side?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Believe me, we were not really interested in that frankly speaking. I really have no idea how many players there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that in our part of the world people play this kind of small-scale soccer with three- to five-member teams?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, three to five if they have the small goals, but then there can be the goalie plus six if they're playing on a handball court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, would you agree that on this photograph there is no handball goal so that it was probably played on that other kind of court?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot see the goal, but that is really your assumption. I have no idea what kind of game they played because I wasn't there to watch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I fully understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, bear in mind that you have only limited time and ask the question that the witness is able to answer. I'm speaking for myself, but I'm having the impression that you are not using your time very efficiently. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your suggestion and advice, but this witness is truly a professional and he's answering 99 per cent of all the questions put to him. So let's not have the photograph returned, but it is a contemporaneous photograph. Anyway, has this statement of Mr. Ismet Fazlic's been admitted at some point or should we admit it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic says that in every team there were five members respect --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 15047 because Dzemo Kazlic [sic] mentions the name and says that there were three on each side, so a total of six players. 65 ter number is 15047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica said he had no knowledge about those facts. What's the point of going on in such a detail with this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd like us to review all the inconsistencies that follow this incident because that is of exceptional importance for the Defence. It doesn't only deal with a reasonable suspicion, but it's supposed to show what it was that actually happened. If you think that that is not needed, maybe we can disregard Dzemo Kazlic [sic] and perhaps we can deal with him when another witness appears if there are going to be witnesses with regard to this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Sabljica, in order to hear the sound of firing, at what distance should these shells have been fired?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you on the basis of my personal experience as a soldier, you have to be pretty close in order to hear the shell being fired because that sound is not as loud as the sound of detonation. You probably know that. I said 50 to 100 metres. Now, the other sounds that witnesses heard, they say that they heard firing. It's very hard. If you are in town and if somebody fires from a position that is out of town, 500, 600 metres away, you can hardly hear the shell actually being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
