utterances.text: Do you agree that if a shell is fired from a distance of that sort, that sound travels faster than the actual shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course a shell is slower than sound, the velocity of sound, I mean really, at least as far as mortars are concerned. That is scientifically proven.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if somebody heard the sound of firing before the sound of explosion, then that had to be within that range that you described. And also, the sound of firing would be heard before the shell actually arrived and before the explosion took place; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me paint a picture for you. At Hrasno Brdo while I was still a soldier of the Army of Republika Srpska [as interpreted], every firing from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, these shells were not directly directed at us because we were 50 to 100 metres away depending on how the line went. However, we could hear firing from some of the artillery pieces. You could not know which one of course and you could hear the shell flying over your positions, and after a while you would hear the explosion. So at least 2 or 3 seconds have to go by by the time you hear this, and if you are close to where the military units are you can actually hear the sound of firing of a shell for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to check if there was an interpretation error. The first part of the witness 's transcript in English reads: "While I was still a member of the Army of Republika Srpska." I want to check if that in fact is what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I mentioned the Army of Republika Srpska because it was from their positions that the firing could be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But now it's some kind of a joint army consisting of three ethnic battalions; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now it is the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's the way it is now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have on this statement of Dzemo Kadric page 3, paragraphs 4 and 5 -- sorry, sorry, just a moment, please. Dzemo Kadric, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dzemo Kadric refers to the names of the players of the other match and then he says: "The match was about to end close to 10.00 ..." Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes, in English, but I can -- [In English] "In the morning suddenly we heard a sound of --" [Interpretation] we heard a sound --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They heard the sound of firing.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Dzemo's statement and I explained this to you. So I would not like to state any views with regard to the statement of some other witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us just state that he heard that and then he says that people were watching the game and they fell on the ground a few seconds after that firing the shell exploded in the centre of the playground. How long would it take for the shell to arrive if you hear the sound and then a few seconds later there is the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, these are parts of a second. By the time you hear this and you lie down, you can ask Mr. Dzemo if he appears in this courtroom. I don't want to state my views in relation to what he had stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this statement be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I made it clear that we cannot admit a third person's statement, and I indicated that this may be a waste of your time, your precious time. Move on to your next topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I thought that this was a witness -- or rather, that this was a document that was obtained by the OTP and it speaks of the incident. But all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recall how far away the line of separation was or the line of conflict unfortunately from the site of this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know because we did not investigate that in our cases. I really don't know what the actual distance was. It was probably very close. You know that Dobrinja was intersected, part was held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and part was held by the Army of Republika Srpska. As far as I can remember, all of that was quite close and the exact distance of the first lines of defence in relation to this playground I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you like us to call up once again this map but section 14, that is 09390C. That's the 65 ter number, section 14, so that we can see how close all of this is. You agree that it couldn't have been more than 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. You are leading me to say how many metres there were, but I really cannot say because I don't know how far away the playing ground was from the line of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please don't hold it against me. The Defence has the right to lead.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not holding it against you. You are well within your rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sheet 14 to -- for the page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this line, what you've been saying now, Dobrinja 4, can you see this, can you see who controls what? Actually, do you see Aerodromsko Naselje that is under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red line denotes the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska and the blue line denotes the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Do you agree that that is the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this map, yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the slopes of Mojmilo up here, the green area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to mark an arrow there and place the letter M to show the direction of Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to draw it on the hill itself, this is M, Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct - and we can see it on the map - that this was under the control of Army of BH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This hill was under BH control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for Aerodromsko Naselje that I had taken to be Dobrinja, to the left can you put A, Aerodromsko Naselje which was under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was under the control of Army of Republika Srpska, A, that's what you meant; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Can you now see where that heating plant is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. If you think it's this building here, I'm not quite sure. Or is it perhaps this one? This is a school. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the site where this incident occurred, can you mark that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could zoom-in if I see the street of Vahide Maglaic perhaps I could be able to tell.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we going to lose this? Are we going to lose the markings if we zoom-in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we can try to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps later you could mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or just could you put the date and signature here and we'll admit this as D758. And then we can zoom-in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This neighbourhood, the upper left-hand corner, can we zoom-in so we can see the street names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further -- no, to the left -- no, no, that's too much. Can we zoom-out once going upward to the left. Can you sort it out, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the map, but I'm trying to find the street Vahide Maglaic. I cannot see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could this map be of assistance, the hard copy? And then with the assistance of this map you can try to mark it on this other one.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Numbers?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably marked with a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you find the number on the back?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 473. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it. And can you see this that says "smoke-stack," you see it says here "smoke-stack"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find this street that I have already found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're looking for Vahide Maglaic; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is marked 473 on this hard copy map and it intersects with the boulevard of Mimar Sinana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, do you have a 65 ter number over map which is appearing in the Sarajevo specific binder, page 10 on which the shelling --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, we'll get that to you right now, the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map you've just shown me, is it with the old names of streets?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's actually new. It says liberators of Sarajevo street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, Liberators of Sarajevo and Hamdije Kapidzica, these are new names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 13581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we use that map for the moment? Let's give it a try. Let's bring up that number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter didn't hear the number but I would like 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the number again, Mr. Gaynor. He lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I'll have it in -- sorry, it was 13581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we zoom-in to number 4. Number 4 should be in the centre. Can you confirm, Mr. Sabljica, that number 4 may be the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because on the street map Vahide Maglaic is under number 473 below the school, further to the south. This is the primary school below the name Dobrinja, and it turns out the street must be parallel with this other street Zikica Spanac according to the street map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this smoke-stack?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the heating plant? But there are several heating plants. There is two that you see next to the Lukavica road. And then you have the first one on the entrance plus another one. I don't know exactly which one of them it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map where Vahide Maglaic Street is according to you and the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this map. I find this street plan of Sarajevo much more helpful because we see 473 marking the street of Vahide Maglaic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that from the site of the incident one of these heating plants is visible?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the one to the north-west from the site of explosion. That means that this place marked "smoke-stack" could be taken as the site of the incident at the playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, Vahide Maglaic fits where?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who made this, but whoever was competent wrote quadrant E7 and number 473.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then mark the heating plant and the direction pointing to the top of Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark Mojmilo with an M and this is the heating plant with T.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And Vahide Maglaic Street is now called the square of Dobrinja children. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It used to be Vahide Maglaic Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case it's number 4 up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the diagonal across this square lies in the north-south direction, this diagonal that goes from the Lukavica road to the top of this building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this or the opposite one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The opposite one. I believe that other one is north-east/south-west.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the boiler plant is north-west from the site of explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just show us exactly this direction which leaves the heating plant a little to the west.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I'm drawing the diagonal here. Shall I mark it with north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we now agree that on three out of four sides the confrontation line is no farther than 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this red line is the confrontation line? If we zoom-out we'll lose the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can sign it and then we'll zoom-out, date, initials.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D759, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Witness, do you see number 39 just below --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you go back to the previous map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Section 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sheet 14 of 9390C. Whatever is okay, marked one. Let's bring up the marked one. Just a second. Can you zoom-in further. Do you recognise -- do you see -- zoom-in further. Do you see the number 39 again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. I see number 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you can tell the distance from this confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some 300, 400 metres away. I agree with Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to mark again the heating plant, this diagonal across the square.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To mark north and all that I did previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heating plant, north, Mojmilo is marked, and the impact is somewhere here. It's marked. And these are the defence lines. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we would be assisted by another photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We need to keep -- need to give a separate number for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D760.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Date and signature then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D760, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we'll be now using a photograph that all the parties have in their e-mail, but it's not yet uploaded in e-court and it would help the witness to identify the broader area. 1D2579. Could we place this photograph on the ELMO and its in everyone's e-mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, let us make good use of the time. Was it established that the calibre of the shells was -- what kind of shells were they?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar shells, 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the minimal distance from which an 82-millimetre shell can be fired?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you from memory, some 600, 650 metres. That's the minimum allowed firing range for these mortars, but it gives the best results at 4200. You may correct me if I'm wrong because it was all a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Everybody has firing tables. Can you recognise this photograph? Can you identify the parking-lot, the heating plant, and Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see the heating plant, Mojmilo, the parking-lot, and the basketball playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where was the match played? According to this man Ismet it was on the playground, according to other people on the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our measurements we found that the shell fell on the parking-lot. You can see that from the photo documentation, and I stand behind that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then mark the playground with PG, mark the parking-lot, and the heating plant.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you can write on this screen with an electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can come back to it later when it's uploaded in e-court. That will be soon. Now, with a 0 charge what is the minimum range for this 82-millimetre mine?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now it's here in e-court. Can you mark the playground, the parking-lot, with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Playing ground, parking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The heating plant and Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Heating plant, Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We agree, don't we, that Mojmilo was under the BH army control?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've established that already. Do you want my signature and date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As usual.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see P1053. P1053.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's just look at page 1 to identify the document and then we'll move to page 57. This is an incident on the 1st of June, 1993. The report was finished on the 7th of July, 1993. It was done for the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's clearly written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: UN commission for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 57 we see that it is a transcript of an interview conducted at the headquarters of the BH Army in Dobrinja on the 5th of July. Do you agree that this interview was conducted with Dinko Bakal?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now look at paragraph 3: "When I heard the detonations, I thought these were mortar shells." Can you continue:

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "However, later we found parts of mortar shell and they were 60-millimetres calibre. Since I had a phone in my apartment, I phoned to the hospital and to the army commander and asked for some ambulances ..." and et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it clear from this that fragments of a 60-millimetre shell were found and you were not informed of that when you came three years later?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see this table of charges to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the 60-millimetre weapon is carried on your back, it's treated as a light weapon?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's used for demining, for destroying smaller targets, and it was good at 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it could be used for a shorter range also?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course if we are really talking about 60 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us stay on the assumption that there was also an 82-millimetre weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D0262 -- 1D02262. Could we zoom-in on this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can't learn it by heart. You have to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that charge 1 can be fired from a distance of 80 metres -- sorry, 0 charge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the basic charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The basic 0 charge can be fired from 80 metres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next charge, number 1?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 metres -- sorry, 225 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree then that possibly 0 charge or charge 1 would be fired even if it's not a 60-millimetre weapon would fall within confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this table with distances, you can see that it can be fired from a smaller distance, but from which place I really can't say, I did not confirm that in my report either. We just established the direction from which it descended, and again we worked on the parking-lot where we were brought three years later and you saw for yourself which shell we dealt with. The shell that is now shown on the playground was not even taken into account by us. We did not work on the playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all -- objection, on two grounds. First of all, notice. This document was not contained on the list of documents provided to the Prosecution at the commencement of cross-examination. And although we have been receiving several e-mails during cross-examination, including one at 11.22 a.m. containing the previous photograph, we have not received any notification of this document. Now, the second ground of objection is that there's no indication as to the source of this document, and we would like to see the original document from which this page is taken in order to verify its authenticity and accuracy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should we put it being marked for identification until the time we would be satisfied as to its foundation, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of help, this is a manual from 1984, Mr. Sabljica knows this very well, it originates from our former country, joint country, and I think that we can help resolve this dilemma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you confirm that, Mr. Sabljica? Would you like to see the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I am familiar with that book and I can confirm that this was published by the JNA and refers to artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like page 85 to be shown to Mr. Sabljica nevertheless. We are going to waste some time on that, but I think it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll mark it for identification pending translation. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit MFI D762, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can arrange that so that the cover page of that book would be uploaded as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like just Mr. Sabljica to confirm that the page 85 is identical to the one that we have just shown in the court.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has a number been assigned? I haven't heard.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D762.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to go back now regardless of your reservation concerning the data contained in the statement, but let us assume that one can hear the firing noise and we know the calibre. Can that help to determine the distance, given that by applying your methods we can only determine the direction and not the distance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The facts that you mentioned concerning the hearing of the firing can help in some general conclusions. If you have radar information, you can know the exact location of the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you find it a bit unusual that the time elapsing between the firing and the blast has never been explained or taken into account; on the other hand, we have two witnesses who had heard the firing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not for the witness to comment upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you had had this data, would you have required that to be established as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't. This is completely irrelevant for our method. This is more in the domain of some personal sensation of witnesses claiming that they heard the noise or didn't hear the noise. So one should take that with some reservation and with a grain of salt. Therefore, we didn't take that into account when compiling our reports. I attributed no importance to anyone's statement to the effect of the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that because you only determined the direction, not the distance?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am reiterating the fact that this is not the only reason. This is something that is not relevant. This is just a subjective opinion given by someone stating that he had heard the firing. We didn't have any equipment or devices that could be used to establish the exact origin of fire and the place of fire. So these subjective statements cannot be taken into account as reliable ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I understand your point of view. But in this trial if we have two people confirming that they heard the fire, the Defence has to take that into account. Would you agree that after three and a half years the traces on the asphalt surface have remained quite visible. Is it possible that someone had tampered with that surface in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not more prominent, but they were -- was some red mass poured over them because all across the town the so-called roses of death were made. However, there was no mechanical intervention. It was only marked in a better and more visible way. You can refer to Mr. van Hecke and his report, where he describes the traces in another incident. So there was no chipping off or any other works that were done on the place of impact. What we have is only the place of impact and the effects caused by the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this filling-in by this red substance intended to preserve the traces? Were the tunnels, for example, filled in with that substance and subsequently was this substance removed in order to use the tunnel for determining the angle?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this marking was only for the purpose of memorials of all those ugly things that had been happening in the past and for posterity to know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in this criminal investigation report, number 9970, 65 ter, 09970.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have it back again and I'd like us to see page 3. The last ERN digits are 658.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the P number of this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian version is all right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is Exhibit P1699.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please find the portion where it says the position of the central crater caused by the --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was fixed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please indicate the portion that they are reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, could you indicate -- could you find that passage from the monitor in the e-court so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have found it in B/C/S and I'll try to find the corresponding passage in English. And in English it should be on the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have it. Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have found it and I can indicate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, you can -- we can find it. Thank you. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This third paragraph, the centre -- no, second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The position of the central crater ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I continue reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and please explain the meaning of this.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The position of the central crater on the Tarmac surface created by explosion of the artillery shell was fixed based on the relation between the arch section and the stairwell (on the eastern side ... which is 4 metres ... and to the central crater which is 11.5 metres, ... photographs 2 and 3 ..." Now let me explain what this means. When we fix the position of explosion taking some solid object as a bench-mark which is not changeable. So in this case we took the stairwell that exists even today, we gauged the distance between the existing building in -- or facility, in this case stairwell, and we took the arc from the stairwell as one measure and the other one was from the edge of the stairwell to the place of explosion. And we used a normal measuring device that every technician has. So whoever comes to the spot can easily find the place where the shell landed. Did you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let us explain where this 4-metre line is. Maybe a sketch would be helpful and can you use any of the photographs that you have to make this sketch?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of the photographs can be used because the stairwell is not shown in them. I'm sorry that there is no sketch of the site that the scene of crime officer makes. So there is no sketch showing the stairwell. If you look at photo 2, which I have in hard copy, which is on the left-hand side of the impact place where you have this soldier standing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the investigation report prepared by the BH police, was there such a sketch included?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There should be one because yesterday we saw one that was drawn by a technician where he made a mistake by marking north wrongly, but you will have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Prosecution to tell me if they by any chance have this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll look into the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the descent angle of the mortar was not established?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. There was no tail fin, there was no fuse. So to be honest when you don't have enough evidence and traces I don't think it would be appropriate to just play around and toy with that. I only -- we only indicated the deviation in degrees with regard to north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Back in 1993 did anyone establish the angle of descent? Were you provided with this kind of material?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally. I repeat, at the time when this incident took place I was in the Army of BH not in the police of BH, and during the subsequent investigation nobody gave us this kind of material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 2 of this document to see what it reads. I believe that this should be the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, next page in English and -- yes, now we have the proper page in B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please focus now on the paragraph which says -- can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Do you want me to read it? "Based on the size of the marks on the Tarmac surface and the shapes of the prominent trails and impact trails of blast, we deduced as follows: "The shell which hit the Tarmac surface of the parking-lot was an 82-millimetre shell. "And the shell came from the south-easterly direction or 110 degrees from the north." Do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The point of impact of the second shell was not forensically examined due to the changed appearance of the soil adjacent to the parking-lot (various agricultural plants have been planted there in the meantime). A photo file was created during the making of this record and it constitutes an integral part of it." And below it says: "Sarajevo, 24th of November ..." And we have the signatures of Mr. Medjedovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, apart from the direction stated in your report, there is no claim that it was fired either from the position of the Army of Republika Srpska or the position of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it for yourself. There is no indication as to which of the two armies could be accused of this particular fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that something was plant in the impact place of the second shell. Do you remember which particular plants were planted there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Throughout the war Sarajevo was besieged and encircled. It was difficult to get any vegetables, and I suppose that they planted tomatoes or potatoes or any other kind of vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that this report is an integral part of the relevant P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that right? Yes, it is. Thank you. Can I please then ask again for P0153 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction:

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1053. Let's first look at page 1 in order to identify the document and then we shall proceed. P1053, that's a Prosecution exhibit that we had already seen before. This is a UN report dated the 7th of July, 1993. Can we please move to page 9 of this document. This was written three years before the work conducted by your team, so could you please read paragraphs 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Paragraph 1: "Splinter pattern indicates mortar, minimum calibre 81-millimetres. Bearing to origin of fire" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can all read this. What is the question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read it to yourself then, Mr. Sabljica, so that you can see what UNPROFOR did at the time.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the second part it says that on the macadam --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No fuse was found and that's why they could not apply the tunnel method, but they do mention this macadam. It's a type of surface, macadam.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has already been admitted, so I just wanted us to have a full picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now it's the time to break, Mr. Karadzic. I have to note for your planning purposes you have spent about five hours and 40 minutes. We allowed you seven minutes to cross-examine the witness -- I'm sorry, seven hours. Which means that you will have one hour and 20 minutes left for the remainder of your cross-examination and that you will have about ten minutes tomorrow to conclude your cross-examination. So I would like you to plan the remainder of your cross-examination to be concluded in that time-limit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I would like to indicate frequent errors, Freudian ones. Mr. Gaynor asked Mr. Sabljica about his participation in the explosion in Markale, and this is the second time that you have been experiencing hours as minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- rise and we'll resume at 12.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that we will have just one question left in relation to the football game.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, we have one crater on the asphalt and that's what they showed you and that's what you measured; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were these holes filled with this red mass?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. After the on-site investigation. It wasn't done before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, so when you were there you didn't have to remove that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We've clarified that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter number 10083.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of expert Richard Higgs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I hear of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to see this. I believe that there should be a version in English. This is a report of Mr. Richard Higgs. On page 8 now, paragraph 1. Mr. Higgs toured these sites in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Sarajevo. And -- I don't want to say this by way of a comment, I don't know if it was tourism or investigation, but nevertheless let's have a look at what he says in paragraph 1. Would you read that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to read it in our language.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we have the original English. This is not the page. It should be C.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Statement of witness Gasi, number 00379300, at the request of the International Court for the former Yugoslavia I toured the location with Mr. Chester Stamp and I examined the two craters ..." et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the relevant page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Serbian version. And in English, yes, 10 -- 7510 are the last digits on the ERN number. It's probably not this, it's not 8. It should be C. So it's C and then the text that follows, the statement of Witness Gasi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's the 7th page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In general we don't see any point in asking Mr. Sabljica to read the document out loud when it's in the English language version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: How is it possible that Mr. Higgs considerably after your investigation saw two craters on the asphalt, both of them filled in with a red substance, when according to your findings one crater was in the soil, a soft surface, and when there was vegetation there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Ask that Mr. Higgs if he comes here. I don't know if these two craters are related to that incident since he mentions red substance. I know that later on the ones in Markale were marked with this red substance. I've already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. He now speaks of what happened at the football-match in Dobrinja. At any rate you find this unusual?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Highly unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that after this was filled in, as Mr. Higgs says, after the crater was filled in with a red substance to a degree a detailed analysis was rendered impossible?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here and I agree; however, part of the crater was preserved and it makes it possible to draw some conclusions. So perhaps some of the traces were removed by that method.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that in our terminology and in our language asphalt and macadam are two different things?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And how.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In our terminology macadam is a cobbled road and --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I said that when I read that report that you asked me to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have shed light on this, and I would like us to move on to the tram incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. The -- could I ask Mr. Karadzic to slow down because in that instance the entirety of Mr. Sabljica's answer was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was not confident which part is answer and which part is question. Could you tell us in a brief manner again about the terminology in your language which relate to asphalt and macadam, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karadzic asked whether in our language that terminology denoted different concepts and my answer was yes, because "macadam" in our language denotes a road that is covered in crushed stone, so it is not the same kind of surface as asphalt. So that is what was stated if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for the speed, but I'm trying to deal with everything in this time that is so limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can we now look at sniper fire against the tram on the 23rd of November, 1994. This is incident number 14 [realtime transcript read in error "13] from table F. Do you remember the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several such incidents involving trams. If you could tell me the approximate location of where the tram was hit, then perhaps I will be able to give you more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter number 09699 and then ERN page 917 -- just a moment, please. ERN 9779. That is the incident that occurred by the technical school between the Marsal Tito barracks and the technical school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the tram was moving in the direction towards the new city; right, Novi Grad, east-west. Is that the incident? Right. I see. I have it in front of me now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this is Exhibit P1714.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please refresh your memory by looking at this.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it right now. Yes, this is the report of a colleague, operative inspector from the homicide department. And I see my own name under number 4 and the tram went to the garage so it could not be returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you a general question now. Automatic fire, bursts of gun-fire from automatic weapons like the ones that we have, like automatic rifles, is there a certain dispersion and can you tell us the relation between dispersion and distance?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The bigger the range, the bigger the dispersion and it depends on the marksman involved. And also in our terminology we say to which side does a rifle move, and if you are firing bursts of gun-fire you can hardly hit a single target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From a distance particularly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the range of these automatic rifles that all three warring parties had?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: APM-70 and APM-72 which were the result of our version of the AK rifle. It was 350 to 400 metres. That was the most efficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that the most efficient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I object to the question: "What is the range of these automatic rifles that all three warring parties had?" I don't believe that Mr. Karadzic elicited evidence from the witness that all three warring parties had a specific kind of rifle. He is assuming a fact which is not necessarily in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Gaynor's observation. Be more specific in putting such terms. Let's move on. Witness answered in any event.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Again, I'm trying to save time. Could the transcript be corrected. I said that the incident number was 14 from list F. It's not 13, as it is stated here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is way too fast for interpretation and for court reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this come from the former JNA? And could you please pause briefly for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. All of this came from the arsenal of the JNA, 95 per cent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that there were also automatic weapons that had silencers for which silencers existed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For example, Heckler & Koch rifles that were used by the special units, that is where silencers were used, yes. That existed, I saw that, so yes there were weapons with silencers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us now what you could conclude here beyond reasonable doubt?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case I see before me a report that was compiled by a colleague from the homicide department, so I don't have the ballistic findings. Since the tram had gone to the garage I -- we could just describe the damage sustained by the tram and we could give indicia of the angles of descent and in terms of the side of the tram that was affected. We could not state our views on the point or the area because the tram was already in the garage and it couldn't go back anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, does this suggest that there had been several bullets, that one person got killed, and that several persons were wounded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here. One person was killed and three persons were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that this person who was killed was hit by three bullets from a burst of gun-fire? That's in the statement of his wife who was wounded herself.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't know about that. I haven't read his wife's statement and that is not what I was interested in as a ballistics man, to examine the corpses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This crime department -- these people from the crime department, could they do anything without ballistic findings? The calibre was not established, nothing was, but they just say that it was the aggressor that had fired the shots. Could they do that without your findings, the ballistic findings?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course that was not possible. You'll have to ask him why it was written that way and on the basis of what he wrote that, on the basis of what particular knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 231194. 1D2415 actually, Google. This is Google, from this area. The statement that we have on the screen, or rather, the official report, has that been admitted in some document. Yes, obviously, it's part of an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me; right ?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, sorry. Can you recognise this area of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see Vrbanja bridge, the Assembly, the main road where vehicles move and where the tram goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this photograph can you mark the place where the incident had occurred? It says here Marsal Tito barracks and the technical school. Can you mark the technical school?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's the technical school. That's the technical school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The complex of the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It starts from here and it goes all the way up there to Pofalici. Tito barracks, that's how I'm going to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall where the incident took place? According to the official report, the tram was between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks, have a look at this, it could have been here, all the way here. Now how can I say exactly, it was right here. I cannot pin-point it but I can mark the area between these two buildings that are referred to. Would you like me to do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you could please shade that area.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here between the technical school and the barracks, a bit more. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Place of incident, could you mark it that way, PI.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to the statement of the tram-driver Huso Pavle [sic], which he gave a day after the incident, the tram was at the U-turn for a new tram stop. Can you mark it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at the intersection of these two streets. That's the turn for the new railway station. I'll put a circle there. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Do you remember or perhaps you can see from this report that the incident happened at 1530 hours?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the report of that inspector? If he says so in the report, then it must have happened at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does your report exist about this incident and why isn't it included? What did your ballistic report say about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you at the beginning, if we had done it we probably just indicated damage on the tram. We were only able to measure the angles and that was all. Since the tram was not in place, we could not do the measurements to determine placement, as I explained earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put the date and your signature there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Sabljica, when modified air bombs first appeared?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was already in 1995, towards the end of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me help you. Do you recall that that was one year into the sanctions imposed by Yugoslavia and that's why they appeared, why they were modified?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reason, but I know that Republika Srpska was under the embargo imposed by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get -- sorry, did this get a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D763.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 09988. Let's see the first page to identify the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit P119.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 8, ERN number -- 830 is the ending of the ERN number. Actually, can we get the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "My name is Huso Palo ..." Can you see this? Now the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean. "On the day when the incident happened"? "There were no military targets in the street, only UNPROFOR and us. It was clear that the civilians were the targets." He mentions the presence of the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I trouble you to look at the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean "additionally"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, he says he lived in Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Additionally, in late 1993 three improvised aircraft bombs fell in the area. They destroyed five houses."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He's talking about Bistrik; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, this witness the day after the incident claims the incident happened in the presence of the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is part of a document offered by the Prosecution. Since there are no findings by you here, we will not spend more time on it although it is full of contradictions that you are not necessarily aware of. Just a moment, please. Relative to the side of the tram, it was established that the projectile could have been fired from south/south-east?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read that in that report you placed on the screen earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Briefly, apart from this general conclusion, nothing else could be established about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you will have to ask the writer of this report how he determined that the direction was south/south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Gaynor asked you in chief about another incident that happened two days later, 25th November, remember, after the stop in Pofalici; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the case of this incident it is again true that the tram was not placed in such a way that the exact origin of fire could be determined?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That case was a bit different. It concerned a distance of about a couple of metres, and we stated it in our report. One green building was suspected, but there was no visual contact established because we could not place the tram exactly where it was. But the cardinal point was determined precisely. We were within a range of 3, 4 metres and the driver's statement helped us. However, we wrote our report with a reservation, saying that it was not possible to establish the exact location without sighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the witness has stated that the UNPROFOR commission investigated the very next day, just as the MUP commission, when the tram was brought again back to approximately the same place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that two witnesses stated that the Frenchman said this was fired from this building, showing the building, in the territory controlled by the BiH army and he said, "If you want me to, I can even show you the window"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, that is something I hear for the first time. I don't know anything about this or who stated it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see this Official Note ERN 03315377.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we place it on the ELMO if it's not available on the screen, but it should be because it's part of the overall report on the incident of 25th November. There are many statements included. Two trams were fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in this investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Both the trams, the numbers were 277 and 217, those were the numbers of the trams.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we place this statement on the ELMO if there is no other option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think this may be part of 65 ter 10512. Your Honours have already admitted two documents from the investigative dossier into this incident. Mr. Karadzic is now dealing with a document which was not one of those admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say, if one number is admitted I would rather have the whole document admitted rather than two papers chosen by the Prosecution. In that case we would be obliged to tender parts of the document, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that it was not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, correct. The precise document that Mr. Karadzic is now dealing with. Now Mr. Karadzic's point is that the entire investigative dossier should be admitted rather than merely the two documents within that dossier which Your Honours have already admitted. And we have no objection to the admission of the entire 65 ter number 10512. Now, for the record the two documents which Your Honours have admitted is P1728. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First of all, let's bring up 65 ter 10512 and see what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the page I need and this is something entirely different. A moment ago the Serbian version was okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a 39-page document, so we will go through. What's the ERN number you have?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 17 of this document. Right. It's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to this Official Note, one of the Official Notes made on this incident. It was done the day after and it says: "The holes created" -- or rather, read the paragraph that begins with: "When I arrived ..." and then we'll discuss --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this Sulejman Pilav? "When I arrived, there were three members of the French contingent of the UNPROFOR at the site. One of them was an interpreter ..." et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you see where it reads "the holes created"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "An UNPROFOR officer pushed metal rods into the bullet-holes and said something to the others in French. The other members of the team did not do or say anything. In response to my question, the interpreter told me that the officer had said that the fire had come from the Muslim side, from the neighbouring white building in Sibenska Street which also houses the Bel Ami bar. The interpreter even said that the officer was able to determine from which window it was fired. The officer then removed the metal rods and left the site with his team at approximately 1745 hours. The tram-driver drove the tram to the depot. "Note compiled by: "Sulejman Pilav."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to tender the entire document or only this page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for the time being this page, but there will be other times when we will tender other pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D764, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this contain a ballistic report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5373, that's the ending of the ERN number in this document. Page 13 of the document itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you remember, I already explained this report when I talked about the damage to the side of the tram, the angle of descent, optical visibility, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the English version page 13 -- or rather, page 14 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this done on the 29th October, four days after the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you describe to us the difficulties with the tram. You had to move the tram around quite a lot to get sighting towards the green building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, we asked that the tram be placed exactly where it was hit according to the witness statements. The first time we did it sighting pointed to this green building as a suspect feature in the territory controlled by the VRS in Grbavica; however, that building did not provide a direct line of sight to the tram and that's written in the report. And then the driver intervened, his name is Aleksandar Guzina, as is written here, and he said the tram needed to be moved 3 or 4 metres further, either backwards or forward. However, we said in our report that there was no direct line of sight and we clearly stated our reservations because for some reason, I can't remember what reason, it was impossible to move the tram where the driver said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The transcript does not include that there was no direct line of sight to provide for a conclusion that targeting was intentional. The witness said that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written in the report and in English as well, and you can see it concerning tram 217. However, in the case of tram 277 it was much easier to establish from which side the shot came from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the next page in English and in Serbian, the very end of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I draw your attention to the words "sighting -- by means of sighting with regard to the penetration points marked as numbers 1 and 2 ..."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A section of the 'white skyscraper' in Lenjinova street was established as the site from which the round may have been fired on the said tram. Photograph number 3. Photographic evidence was established ..." et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you establish that a shot could have been fired from that skyscraper, but did you establish that it was fired from the skyscraper?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were doing the on-site investigation, it was not quite possible, but if we recall the first day of my evidence we had occasion to see the sniper emplacements on that building which we considered suspect and there was strong evidence, strong indications in the case of this tram, that it could indeed be the place from which the shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor asked you on page 79 of the transcript whether you had found evidence or indications that the shots may have been fired also from the side held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not find such evidence. My team did not find it. I would not like to comment on the work of the French team. They are better placed to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you given an assignment to rule out the positions of the BH Army? You did not find them, but were you looking for them? Was your assignment given to you that you should rule out the positions of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say with full responsibility that no, we worked without any pressure from anyone from any political or military organisations. We did the work of civilian police, forensic experts, but in the difficult conditions of war. And we did not do the sighting influenced by anything. We did not consider any party to the conflict guilty in advance for any killing or any wounding from a fire-arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Certainly. I am not blaming anyone. I just want to know what exactly your mission was. Mr. Gaynor said on page 79, line 25: [In English] "Is there anything in this document to suggest that you concluded that the tram had been fired upon by Bosnian government forces?" [Interpretation] Was your task to either confirm or rule out the positions of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, nobody ever gave us such a task.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please call up sheet 10 or section 10 of the map, 65 ter 0939C.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'm sorry that I'm dealing with an incident that is not covered by the indictment, but Mr. Gaynor dealt with it in examination-in-chief and my cross-examination is very much related to it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Section number 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that can we have Mr. Medjedovic and Mr. Sabljica's report admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Medjedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Medjedovic. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think this is part of what we have already admitted as P1728. I should stand corrected if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct according to our records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the eastern portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the Pofalici stop or do we need to look at number 11?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like you to zoom-in on the upper left-hand corner -- or rather, upper right-hand corner. And you have to move the map further to the east.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then have section 11. Yes, this is sheet 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this part now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we zoom-in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where it says "Novo Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To the left -- let's -- and then -- yes, I think that will do. No, do not move to the right. Just go back to the left. Yes. Is it okay, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark, for example, the secondary school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here above number 16. I will mark it with the letters EC, which stands for the school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the building where Belami [phoen] is housed.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is this long building here and I will put letter B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
