utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now mark the place where the incident took place as accurately as you possibly can.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately it happened here. I will mark the general area up to the intersection between Bratstvo, Jedinstvo, and Vojvode Putnika streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark the green building that was originally suspected as the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot do that. I know that on the other side there is 27 July street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the place of incident with number 1 because previously you used letters.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw a parallel green line indicating Wilson's promenade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This exchange is too fast. We cannot cope. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Interpreters couldn't follow you from a while ago because you were so fast. So we have number 1, we'll start from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the incident place, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's suppose that it is in this map at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This street which is now called Hamdije Camelica [phoen] street used to be called Bratstvo Jedinstvo street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the Bratstvo and Jedinstvo bridge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the Bratstvo and Jedinstvo bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You marked the school of economics with a green circle and number 16; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since everything else seems to be marked, tell me what this blue line along the Wilson's promenade signified?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It signifies the defence line of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did the units defend themselves there? How were they deployed? Did they build trenches and were they deployed in buildings, residential buildings, as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection. I don't think this is for this witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, that was the area of the unit that Mr. Sabljica was a member of, that was the 101st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you answer the question, if you can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I'll answer the question. We had both trenches and indoor positions, that is to say in the cellars of the mechanical engineering faculty, the school of economics, and another faculty building, and we had exits that connected them with the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Army of Republika Srpska fortify themselves in a similar fashion and did they defend themselves in the same way, by using trenches along the river and firing positions in cellars?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that because I wasn't at Grbavica during the war, but I can only assume that that was the case. There was no other alternative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, the Wilson's promenade stretches from Bratstvo Jedinstvo as far as the Vrbanja bridge. Can you mark it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we have the inscription "Vilsonovo Setaliste," promenade, we do not need to mark it. Now, can you please put a circle around the Unioninvest building close to the Vrbanja bridge.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was the control of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the case according to this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, had you ever had an opportunity to investigate what we call sniping incidents that took place along the Wilson's promenade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a building close to the Vrbanja bridge a little girl was killed in a flat, and I think that was part of the General Milosevic's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That happened inside the flat?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this little girl was shot inside the flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But outdoors where you can see the civilians, did you carry out any investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when there was a conflict going on nobody strolled up and down the Wilson's promenade. You couldn't even see a bird flying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We shall see about that -- see the documents of BH Army. Can you put the line indicating the streets Franjo Racko and Djure Danicic. So Djure Danicic street is between the Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franjo Racko and Djure Danicic, should I put letters FR and DD.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you cannot mark the suspect green building, can you mark the high-rise building at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that and I'll place the letter N, which stands for skyscraper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If one assumes that fire came, which kind of range and what degrees would you attach to this but provided you were not able to position the tram where it was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't speculate. It says the angle was with respect to the side of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you definitely agree that between this high-rise building and the incident place there were both positions of the BH Army and the Army of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. One can see that, it's so obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a tram that had its windows shut because it was cold, was it possible for one to hear shots coming from this skyscraper or would these shots be better heard from the building where Belami was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be hard to hear any kind of gun-shots in a closed tram. You know how loud trams are. I don't think that they heard the gun-shots at all. They felt the impact when the tram was hit, those who were hit in the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put a U by the Unioninvest building and then the date and your signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D765, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm going to ask whether we are going to be working until 2.00 then, are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it's impossible. Another Bench is sitting today. We have to rise at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1958 then. 1D1958.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to have us identify this together. This is a bulletin from the time when you left the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I left a month before this. This is the 29th of July, so that would be it roughly. I had already joined the police by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces, the security department. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is what is written on this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 26th of July, 1993, a group of civilians at the Wilson promenade were cutting trees in front of the positions of HVO units. It is indicative that the aggressor was not firing, although they had clearly visible objectives before them. The soldiers of the HVO drove away the civilians at the intervention of the soldiers of the 10th bbr and the aggressor opened fire only after the civilians had left." Do you want me to read the rest?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, the rest doesn't matter. Do you agree that this is a document of the intelligence service of our adversaries at the time, and they noted that the Serbs could fire across the river whenever they wanted to but they started firing only when the civilians had left?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what is written here. You can see it for yourself. That's the only thing that I can confirm, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think the witness actually added anything material to the document itself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document does speak of developments at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We agree with Mr. Gaynor's information. Five minutes to conclude for today, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, may I ask you who we should catch and bring in here to have this document admitted? Mr. Sabljica was there, he's familiar with the area and their own intelligence service, military intelligence service, says this. He deals with the same developments like the ones that have been dealt with so far, firing at civilians. So there is no Holiday Inn, there are no journalists, nobody could see this. They could have killed everyone, they did not. So this does speak of what was happening and it speaks of the situation as it was. We should perhaps catch Halilovic or someone to tell us about this and bring them here but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, this is -- you've had a ruling from the President and he's told you to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now, all -- the points raised by the Prosecution is that it is not appropriate to admit this document through this witness. There may be other ways for you to tender it. Even you can consider a bar table motion if necessary. Move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I would like to ask that the Defence be given the possibility to reply to everything stated by the Prosecution before a decision is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have to deal with Markale a bit as well, although I'm convinced that you did not take part in the explosion. You took part in the investigation of the explosion. Isn't that right? I'm referring to the slip of the tongue made by Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I took part in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter number 09622.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1708.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, can you tell us when you arrived and at whose orders. When did you arrive to Markale market?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kanlic, Asim was the name of the investigating judge who ordered us to come and we arrived at 1325 hours and we worked until 1600 hours, and that is what it says here in the report that you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was after the incident, but how much time had elapsed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was less than an hour, 55 minutes, because what happened happened at 20 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that an investigation is supposed to start as soon as possible so that the findings would be as accurate as possible?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the circumstances involved, how fast you can get there. But I do agree in principle, yes, it's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you arrived had the evacuation already taken place of the wounded and the dead?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the evacuation had been completed and there were no wounded or killed persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to your own observations, in which part of the market could there have been the highest concentration of people and goods?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I didn't really pay attention to that. I think that throughout the market there were some goods, some things were being sold. Usually that was the only place where people could buy alcohol, oil, sugar, things that could not -- were in short supply in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the street of the 22nd of December that is up there neighbouring Dzenetica Cikma, so it links Dzenetica Cikma and Tito street. Do you remember that even outside the stalls there were lots of goods that were being sold on the sidewalk in front of the vendors? That's the way it is until the present day as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, people sell all sorts of things. It was cigarettes that were being sold mostly at the time and also some vegetables and cardboard boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you observe, apart from alcohol and tobacco, what other goods were dominant in the market?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sugar, oil, I don't know, some vegetables, different kinds of goods because at the time under such circumstances this market was no longer a classical green market. You could find supplies that were in short supply in town. I'm referring to sugar, oil, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there any time left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll stop here. We'll adjourn for today. I'd like to remind you, Mr. Karadzic, it is your responsibility to pass on to the Prosecution as well as to the Chamber the list of documents you are going to use during the cross-examination before your cross-examination begins. I just tell you that it is totally inappropriate for you to disclose every ten minutes through e-mail the list of new documents as if we are being drip fed. Bear that in mind in the future. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00 and you will have about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just say a word. I fully accept your criticism, but the tempo and rhythm of this trial is such that my whole team is totally beaten and I am just asking for understanding from the opposite side, and I promise that the Defence will display the same degree of understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of October, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
